transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… work, mostly. I’m a cashier, and I’ve been doing some odd things at the register—getting stuck, tapping the scanner in a pattern, or just freezing with my hand over the cash drawer while someone’s waiting. Last week I got written up for it, so… I came in.
When you get stuck or tap the scanner in a pattern, do you feel like you have to do it to stop something bad from happening?

I don’t really know if it’s to stop something bad. It’s more like… I just get stuck doing it. Like tapping the scanner that way, or freezing with my hand over the drawer even though the customer’s right there waiting. It doesn’t fit, and I know that. It got me written up last week.
Right before you tap the scanner or freeze, do you feel a build-up of tension or an urge that gets relieved when you do it?

Not really sure. It’s not like I notice a build-up and then feel better after. I just… end up doing it, tapping the scanner or freezing there with the drawer, and it doesn’t fit what’s happening. Then the customer’s waiting, and I know it looks bad.
When you freeze at the register, do you stay fully aware of what’s going on around you?
I mean… I’m there. I know the customer’s waiting, I know my hand’s just kind of stuck there by the drawer. It’s not like I’m somewhere else. It just… doesn’t match what I’m supposed to be doing.
Do unwanted thoughts keep popping into your mind before this happens?
I haven’t really noticed thoughts like that. It’s more just… it happens, and then I realize I’m stuck there.
Can you hold back the tapping or freezing for a little while if you really try?

Not really. I can tell myself to stop, but when I’m at the register it just kind of… happens. Like the tapping or my hand just stays there over the drawer, even though the customer’s waiting. I don’t seem to catch it in time.
When you tap the scanner or hold your hand over the drawer, does it feel like you have to keep doing it until it feels just right?

Not really “just right,” no. It’s more like I’m just doing something that doesn’t fit—tapping the scanner or my hand just… staying over the drawer while they’re waiting. I don’t have a reason for it. It just happens.
Do you also ever make sudden movements or sounds that happen on their own, like blinking, jerking, sniffing, or throat-clearing?
I don’t think so. Not that I’ve noticed, anyway. It’s not like blinking or making noises… at least I wouldn’t say that.
Growing up, did you often have trouble understanding other people socially, like reading facial expressions or knowing how to join in conversations?
I’m not really sure. I don’t remember having a big problem with that… I was maybe quiet, but I don’t know about reading faces or joining in.
Do you have any very intense interests that you focus on much more than most people do?
Not really. I mean, I watch things or read about things sometimes, but I wouldn’t say it’s intense or anything… not more than other people, I don’t think.
Do these episodes ever stop or lessen when your attention is pulled to something else?

Sometimes, yeah. If someone says something to me or I have to answer a question, it can sort of break it. But at the register I still get stuck sometimes… like tapping the scanner or just freezing there with my hand over the cash drawer. It’s been enough that I got written up last week.
Did these tapping or freezing episodes start around a particularly stressful time in your life?
Yeah… I guess so. It’s been kind of building for, I don’t know, about two years and a few months. Around when my youngest left the Eastern Shore for college.
When you freeze or start tapping, is there a specific unwanted thought in your mind that you’re trying to get rid of?
I don’t think so. It’s not like there’s one thought I’m trying to push out. Sometimes my mind just… catches, I guess. I haven’t really noticed a specific thing.
